speaker: Patient
text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Venous Stasis Ulcer secondary to chronic venous insufficiency.

The history of a 6-month non-healing wound on the right lower leg, combined with 10 years of chronic bilateral leg swelling and a prior deep vein thrombosis, strongly suggests venous stasis. The positive family history further supports a hereditary predisposition to venous valve incompetence. Given the chronic nature and risk factors, I will request a Venous Duplex Ultrasound to confirm reflux or obstruction before initiating compression therapy.
